title: Equivariant Yoneda equation and evaluation on free profinite action spaces
statement:
Work in compatible universes and small skeletons [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $J$ be a compact Hausdorff totally disconnected topological group, let $P$ be the profinite site with finite jointly surjective covers [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], and let $P_J$ have profinite continuous left $J$-spaces, continuous equivariant maps and finite jointly surjective covers [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Write $H(S)=J\times S$ with left translation on $J$, and $tS=S$ with trivial action [def-sfb-profinite-action-parameters]. Put $\mathscr E=\operatorname{Sh}(P)$ and let $\mathscr E^{\underline J}$ be the category of internal actions: a sheaf $X$ with a natural unital associative action $C(S,J)\times X(S)\to X(S)$ [lem-sfb-action-topos-geometric-restriction]. Write $h_T(S)=C(S,T)$, with the induced action when $T\in P_J$. For every $X\in\mathscr E^{\underline J}$ the presheaf
$$\Phi(X)(T)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathscr E^{\underline J}}(h_T,X)$$
is a sheaf on $P_J$. Put $\alpha_T:J\times T\to T$, $(j,t)\mapsto jt$, $\pi_T:J\times T\to T$, and $\gamma:J\times T\to J$, the projections. Evaluation at the identity of $T$ identifies $\Phi(X)(T)$ with
$$Q_X(T)=\{x\in X(T):X(\alpha_T)x=\gamma\cdot X(\pi_T)x\text{ in }X(J\times T)\}.$$
This is an equality of sections on the whole profinite parameter $J\times T$, not merely an equality on ordinary points. On an equivariant map $u:T\to T'$ the restriction is $X(u)$ on these subsets; on an equivariant sheaf map $v:X\to Y$ it is $v_T$. Thus $\Phi$ is a functor to $\operatorname{Sh}(P_J)$. There is a natural bijection
$$e_{X,S}:\Phi(X)(H(S))\xrightarrow{\sim}X(S),\qquad b\longmapsto b_S(1,\operatorname{id}_S).$$
Its inverse sends $x\in X(S)$ to the sheaf map whose component on a profinite $V$ sends $(a:V\to J,b:V\to S)$ to $a\cdot b^*x$. Both bijections are natural in equivariant maps $X\to Y$ and in continuous parameter maps; under $e$, postcomposition by $v$ is $v_S$.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-profinite-action-finite-cover-site], every $h_T:V\mapsto C(V,T)$ is a sheaf on $P$, including $h_J$. Pointwise multiplication makes $h_J=\underline J$ a group sheaf, and $(a,f)\mapsto(v\mapsto a(v)f(v))$ makes $h_T$ an internal action: naturality, identity and associativity hold componentwise. Apply [lem-galois-yoneda-hom-bijection] on the category $P$ to the underlying presheaf of $X$. Since sheaf morphisms are precisely natural transformations [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], evaluation identifies all underlying maps $b:h_T\to X$ with $x=b_T(\operatorname{id}_T)\in X(T)$. Its inverse is $b^x_V(f)=f^*x$: naturality gives $b_V(f)=X(f)b_T(\operatorname{id}_T)$, so these are inverse. Internal equivariance means $b_V(af)=a\cdot b_V(f)$ for every profinite $V$, $a:V\to J$ and $f:V\to T$ [lem-sfb-action-topos-geometric-restriction].

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent-written auxiliary argument; representables and ordinary Yoneda, Stacks categories.tex Tag 001P (lemma-yoneda).

proof.text: For the map $b^x$ of step 1, equivariance implies the displayed equation by taking $V=J\times T$, $a=\gamma$ and $f=\pi_T$: their pointwise action is $\alpha_T$, hence $\alpha_T^*x=\gamma\cdot\pi_T^*x$. Conversely pull that equality back along the continuous map $(a,f):V\to J\times T$. Naturality of the internal action gives $(af)^*x=a\cdot f^*x$ for every $V,a,f$, which is exactly equivariance of $b^x$. Thus the Yoneda bijection restricts to $\Phi(X)(T)\cong Q_X(T)$; the test is an equality of sections on $J\times T$ itself.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent-written auxiliary argument; universal-parameter equivariance test.

proof.text: For an equivariant continuous $u:T\to T'$, precomposition by $h_u:h_T\to h_{T'}$ gives restriction on $\Phi$. The two identities $u\alpha_T=\alpha_{T'}(\operatorname{id}_J\times u)$ and $u\pi_T=\pi_{T'}(\operatorname{id}_J\times u)$ show, by pulling back the equation for $x'\in Q_X(T')$, that $u^*x'\in Q_X(T)$. Step 1 identifies this restriction with $X(u)$. For an equivariant sheaf map $v:X\to Y$, naturality with $\alpha_T,\pi_T$ and equivariance with $\gamma$ send the equation for $x$ to that for $v_Tx$. This is postcomposition on $\Phi$. Restrictions compose by the presheaf law; postcompositions compose by composition of sheaf maps and commute with restrictions. Hence $X\mapsto\Phi(X)$ is a functor to presheaves on $P_J$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent-written auxiliary argument; functoriality and the two Yoneda naturalities.

proof.text: Let $\{p_i:T_i\to T\}$ be a finite jointly surjective equivariant cover and let $x_i\in Q_X(T_i)$ agree on $T_i\times_TT_j$. The underlying cover and overlaps are those of $P$ by [lem-sfb-profinite-action-finite-cover-site]. The sheaf axiom [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] for $X$ gives a unique $x\in X(T)$ with $p_i^*x=x_i$. The maps $\operatorname{id}_J\times p_i:J\times T_i\to J\times T$ are a finite jointly surjective cover of $P$ (a lift of $t$ lifts $(j,t)$ with the same $j$). Pulling $\alpha_T^*x$ and $\gamma\cdot\pi_T^*x$ back along these maps gives $\alpha_{T_i}^*x_i$ and $\gamma_i\cdot\pi_{T_i}^*x_i$, respectively, since each $p_i$ is equivariant. Explicitly, for $r_i=\operatorname{id}_J\times p_i$, one has $\alpha_T r_i=p_i\alpha_{T_i}$, $\pi_T r_i=p_i\pi_{T_i}$ and $\gamma r_i=\gamma_i$. Thus $r_i^*(\alpha_T^*x)=\alpha_{T_i}^*x_i=\gamma_i\cdot\pi_{T_i}^*x_i=r_i^*(\gamma\cdot\pi_T^*x)$. Injectivity of the sheaf equalizer map for the cover $\{r_i\}$ makes the original sections equal. Thus $x\in Q_X(T)$, and uniqueness in $X(T)$ gives uniqueness in $Q_X(T)$. For an empty cover $T=\varnothing$, both $X(T)$ and $X(J\times T)$ are singletons, so the same argument applies. This proves the sheaf condition for $\Phi(X)$, and step 3 now defines the required sheaf-valued functor.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent-written auxiliary argument; explicit descent of the equation, using Stacks sites.tex Tag 00VM (definition-sheaf-sets).

proof.text: For $S\in P$, use $H(S)=J\times S$ with left translation [def-sfb-profinite-action-parameters]. Given $x\in X(S)$, define $B^x_V(a,b)=a\cdot b^*x$. For $r:W\to V$, naturality of the action gives $r^*B^x_V(a,b)=(a\circ r)\cdot(b\circ r)^*x=B^x_W(a\circ r,b\circ r)$, so this is a sheaf map $h_{H(S)}\to X$. For every $c:V\to J$, $B^x_V(ca,b)=(ca)\cdot b^*x=c\cdot(a\cdot b^*x)=c\cdot B^x_V(a,b)$, by associativity. It is therefore equivariant. Evaluating on $(1,\operatorname{id}_S)$ gives $1\cdot x=x$, by the identity axiom.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent-written auxiliary argument; construction of the inverse to free-parameter evaluation.

proof.text: Conversely, let $B:h_{H(S)}\to X$ be equivariant and put $x=B_S(1,\operatorname{id}_S)$. For any $V$, $a:V\to J$ and $b:V\to S$, naturality along $b$ gives $B_V(1,b)=b^*x$. Since $(a,b)=a\cdot(1,b)$ in $h_{H(S)}(V)$, equivariance gives $B_V(a,b)=a\cdot b^*x$. Thus $B=B^x$, proving that $e_{X,S}$ and the construction of step 5 are inverse. If $v:X\to Y$ is equivariant, then $v_V(a\cdot b^*x)=a\cdot b^*v_S(x)$ and evaluation of $vB$ is $v_S(x)$. If $f:S'\to S$, precomposition by $h_{H(f)}$ sends $B^x_V(a,b)$ to $a\cdot(fb)^*x=B^{f^*x}_V(a,b)$. Hence the free bijection is natural in both variables with the stated action on morphisms. The general $Q$ bijection has the same two naturalities by step 3.

lean.note: Uses the already published small profinite-site models and internal-action definitions; does not use the coherent-presentation equivalence or its existence theorem. The helper phi constructs the actual sheaf-valued functor from the asserted descent proof, without any choice.
